self_match_floor_finding.requirement: Telegraph's node requires worst_self_match of at least 0.75: a ground-truth answer scored against itself must be recognised as correct. Registration 496 was rejected on this and on nothing else.
self_match_floor_finding.cause_one: Eight zero-returning paths ran ahead of the exact-match short-circuit in evaluate: input limits, malformed JSON, a time in the answer absent from the question, keyword stuffing, contradictory truth polarity and contradictory probability. Every one is a check on the text itself, so each fires identically when the answer and the ground truth are the same text. Any ground truth tripping one scored 0.0000 against itself.
self_match_floor_finding.cause_two: At the ABI boundary read_input rejects invalid UTF-8 and rank_answer returns 0 without calling evaluate. Correct for an unreadable miner answer, wrong when that answer is byte-for-byte the ground truth. A byte-level comparison now runs before UTF-8 validation.
self_match_floor_finding.prior_design_overridden: A test named exact_matches_do_not_bypass_safety_gates asserted the opposite behaviour deliberately, that a self-match scores 0.0 when the ground truth is itself defective. The intent was sound but the node overrides it, and the node is right: scoring an answer and auditing a fixture are different jobs, and penalising the miner who reproduced the ground truth verbatim punishes the wrong party for the fixture's defect. The test now asserts the corrected contract.
self_match_floor_finding.missed_signal: The third-party harness at zkasuran/telegraph-salience-scorer had been reporting this for two days as 'non-text ground truth self-matches score=0.0000'. It was recorded as pre-existing and set aside while attention went to attack ordering. It was the one structural gate failing, and structural gates are pass-or-reject rather than scored, so it outranked every ordering improvement made in that time.
self_match_floor_finding.limit_recorded: The short-circuit returns before the time-window, stuffing, polarity and probability checks, so their flags are not set on a self-match; those checks are skipped rather than overridden. Flags raised earlier, such as malformed JSON, are still reported. Preserving the later flags would mean threading a self-match condition through six rejection paths for diagnostics nothing consumes.
self_match_floor_finding.regression_caught_in_flight: The first version of the ABI short-circuit validated only the ground truth and the answer, so an over-cap question returned 1.0 instead of 0 and TestInputByteBoundaries failed. It now bounds-checks all three inputs.

overfitting_finding.what_the_series_shows: Local ranking quality improved monotonically across these builds while the external measure went neutral, neutral, then down. Generated-pair inversions fell from 66 of 375 to 9 of 375 and all ten handwritten pools went from 7 separated with 1 tie and 2 inversions to 10 separated with none, and across the same span Telegraph's per-case win count went 31, 31, 31, 28. The entity-binding, ordinal and weather-classifier fixes were neutral against their fixtures. The two changes in registration 98 were actively harmful.
overfitting_finding.leading_mechanism: Both changes made after 96 convert a signal that previously capped a score into one that zeroes it: relation_mismatch was promoted from ambiguous_or_stuffed, which applies score.min(0.49), to contradicted, which returns zero, and question_entity_slot_substituted returns zero as well. A correct answer that trips either rule falls from a capped score that could still beat its paired wrong answer to zero, which loses the case. The score standard deviation rising from 0.29768366 to 0.33863735 is consistent with more answers being driven to zero.
overfitting_finding.why_local_measurement_did_not_catch_it: The ranking pools and the generated pairs were written by us, so a rule that fires only on shapes we did not think of is invisible to them. Both new rules were validated against 53 native tests, 88 factual pairs, 27 fixture cases, 10 pools and 375 generated pairs, and all of them agreed the change was an improvement or neutral. The benchmark is a sound regression guard for properties we chose and is not a proxy for hidden fixtures.
overfitting_finding.correction_to_earlier_reasoning: The tie hypothesis recorded under cross_registration_finding predicted that fixing a tie would move the win count up. The count moved down. That does not confirm or refute the hypothesis about the one originally failing case, because the same build introduced two zeroing rules whose harm could mask any gain, but it does mean the hypothesis is untested rather than supported.
overfitting_finding.implication: Registration 96's scoring behaviour is the best externally measured state, at 31 of 32 tied with 41 and 19. Reverting the two zeroing changes is the action indicated by the only measurement that is actually scored. Doing so will make the local ranking numbers worse: the authorship_entity_swap tie and the shared_token_distractor inversion both return. That conflict is real and the external measure is the one that decides promotion.
overfitting_finding.rule_going_forward: Do not tune the scorer against locally authored corpora without a held-out check. A hard zero is especially dangerous, because it can only ever remove a win that a capped score might have kept. Prefer a cap over a zero unless the contradiction is certain.

cross_registration_finding.observation: Three structurally different scorer builds produced an identical 31 of 32 per-case ordering result against a champion that wins 32 of 32.
cross_registration_finding.why_it_is_informative: Registration 96 changed scoring behaviour substantially against 41: whole answer classes moved from 0.862500 to 0.000000 through question_entity_substituted, an inserted-ordinal penalty was added, and a weather-classifier over-trigger that was applying a probability ceiling to correct general-knowledge answers was removed. Local generated inversions fell from 66 of 375 to 9 of 375. None of that moved the per-case win count. The aggregate margin moved in both directions across the series while the win count never did, which is evidence that the single failing case is not an instance of any inversion class fixed so far.
cross_registration_finding.leading_hypothesis: The failing case is a tie rather than an inversion. Telegraph's wording is that the scorer must rank the good answer *above* the bad one, so an equal score is not a win. The scorer applies hard ceilings via score.min(0.49) and score.min(0.30), and a hard ceiling collapses every answer above it onto one value. Measured on the local ranking pools, the authorship_entity_swap pool ties a correct answer against a wrong one at exactly 0.490000, and four distinct candidates share that value. Clamps are structural and were never touched by any of the three builds, which fits an invariant single-case failure.
cross_registration_finding.hypothesis_status: Unconfirmed against Telegraph's fixtures, which are hidden and whose per-case scores they have stated cannot be disclosed. Supported only by the local reproduction of the same mechanism.
cross_registration_finding.implied_fix: Make the ceilings order-preserving rather than flattening: map scores that exceed a triggered ceiling into a narrow monotone band ending at that ceiling, so two defective answers of different quality stay distinguishable while both remain capped. This helps only where the pre-clamp ordering is already correct; where it is not, a tie becomes an inversion, which is no worse for Stage 2 but no better either. Not yet implemented.
cross_registration_finding.note_on_priority: Telegraph's team stated the objective is ranking quality across the network rather than winning the canonical-script slot. This defect serves both readings: a scorer that assigns a correct and a wrong answer the same score cannot rank them at all, so fixing it is ranking work rather than fixture chasing.

champion_baseline_comparison.what_it_is: Telegraph's production scoring module, published by the team as the intended path for closing the gap locally rather than reverse-engineering hidden fixtures. It is not a rule engine: it embeds question, ground truth and answer with MiniLM-L6-v2 and blends cosine similarity with BM25 and a length signal.
champion_baseline_comparison.composite: 0.25 * cosine(question, answer) + 0.50 * cosine(ground_truth, answer) + 0.15 * bm25(ground_truth, answer) + 0.10 * sigmoid((answer_len - 50) / 20), clamped to [0,1]. Exports alloc, dealloc, rank_answer, plus breakdown_answer, embed, cosine_sim and bm25_score. Built with --features real_weights it is 24,184,674 bytes against our 55,089.
champion_baseline_comparison.harness_validated: Driven through our existing wazero probe, same ABI. Real weights confirmed working rather than the repo's projection fallback: a true paraphrase with almost no lexical overlap, 'Everest is the highest peak on the planet.' against the truth 'Everest is the tallest mountain on Earth.', scores 0.693950 while unrelated text scores 0.059760. Projection mode could not produce that.
champion_baseline_comparison.architectural_difference: Ours is a hand-written lexical and entity-binding rule engine with discrete penalties; theirs is a semantic model with a smooth composite. That difference explains the registration series: our entity-binding, ordinal and weather-classifier fixes were neutral against fixtures judged by a scorer whose primary signal is embedding similarity, because none of those fixes touched semantic coverage.

measured_complementarity.champion_solves_what_we_declared_out_of_: Predicate substitution. Against 'Nile is known as the longest river in Africa.', the champion scores the correct paraphrase 0.704282 above the wrong 'deepest river' at 0.654421. Ours inverts it, 0.804167 against 0.827083. This was recorded as needing synonymy the module cannot judge; a sentence transformer judges it directly.
measured_complementarity.we_are_sharper_where_our_rules_fire: Entity swap in a preserved frame. Against 'Yes, Everest is the tallest mountain on Earth.', both rank the correct paraphrase first, but the champion's margin is 0.059603 where ours is 0.370000.
measured_complementarity.champion_weakness_found: Entity substitution combined with verbosity. Against 'Paris is the capital of France.', the wrong verbose answer 'Lyon is the capital of France, and that is the established answer, well documented in the record...' scores 0.609420, above every correct answer including a bare 'Paris.' at 0.527878. Ours scores the same pair 0.334375 against 0.781250. A judge that prefers a confident wrong verbose answer to a correct terse one is exploitable by exactly that behaviour.
measured_complementarity.length_signal_is_not_simply_gameable: Padding a correct answer with content-free filler lowers the champion's score rather than raising it, 0.527878 down to 0.338312 across four padding levels, because embedding dilution at weight 0.50 outweighs the length term at weight 0.10. An earlier prediction that padding would farm the length signal was wrong.

champion_baseline_comparison.fairness_caveat: The champion inverts 8 of our 10 ranking pools where our module inverts 1. That number must NOT be read as evidence that our module is the better judge. Those pools were authored by us and deliberately built around the failure modes of a lexical scorer, so they are adversarial toward surface-similarity judging in general. Treating that 8 versus 1 as a quality verdict would repeat exactly the overfitting error recorded under overfitting_finding, in the opposite direction.
champion_baseline_comparison.what_this_unlocks: A held-out signal. Until now local ranking numbers could improve while the scored result went 31, 31, 31, 28, with no way to tell overfitting from progress. The champion can now be run locally on unlimited inputs, and breakdown_answer decomposes its verdict into relevance, correctness, lexical and length, so a disagreement can be attributed to a signal rather than guessed at.
champion_baseline_comparison.indicated_direction: Neither architecture dominates. The champion has broad semantic coverage with thin margins, typically 0.005 to 0.06 on cases it gets right, and is weak on entity substitution. Ours has wide margins where its rules fire and is blind where they do not. A judge that combined a semantic signal for paraphrase coverage with discrete contradiction rules for entity binding would beat either, which is presumably why the team published theirs as a starting point. Not attempted; it is an architectural decision rather than a fix.
champion_baseline_comparison.upstream_note: Their README records that cargo test does not run their unit tests, because the unconditional #[panic_handler] in allocator.rs clashes with std on the native target, and states the fix as gating it behind #[cfg(not(test))]. Not reported or offered; noted only so it is not rediscovered.

length_signal_investigation.prompted_by: Telegraph confirmed on 2026-08-20 that the baseline's length term is a real and known limitation, rewarding longer wrong answers over shorter correct ones, and asked that a fix be considered. They also added an MIT LICENSE to the baseline repository on request, which removes the blocker on building from their code.
length_signal_investigation.method: Three variants of their module were built and measured rather than reasoning about which is right: v0 the shipped sigmoid((len - 50) / 20) bonus, v1 the term held constant which is rank-equivalent to removing it, and v2 a penalty-only signal where any answer up to 1.5x the ground truth's length scores full marks and only excess beyond that is penalised.
length_signal_investigation.acceptance_corpus: fixtures/scorer_length_cases.json, four pairs in both directions. Two where a verbose wrong answer must lose to a concise correct one, and two where a legitimately longer correct answer must beat a terse wrong one, so a fix cannot pass by trading one failure for the other.

results.v0_shipped_bonus: Fails 2 of 4. Paris/Lyon at -0.0815 and Tokyo/Osaka at -0.1524.
results.v1_term_held_constant: Fails 1 of 4. Paris/Lyon becomes a bare +0.0074 but Tokyo/Osaka still fails at -0.0648. Removing the bonus is therefore NOT sufficient, because cosine and BM25 also favour the answer that reuses the ground truth's phrasing; only actively penalising excess verbosity overcomes it. This is a more precise diagnosis than remove-or-cap.
results.v2_penalty_only: Passes 4 of 4, at +0.1074 and +0.0352, while the legitimately long correct answers still win at +0.3458 and +0.0704, so it does not over-correct.
results.heldout_effect: All three variants order 3 of 30 held-out pairs correctly. The length fix is neutral on ranking generalisation, which was one of the acceptance conditions.

length_signal_investigation.recommendation: Penalty-only. Reached by measurement rather than by preference, which was the explicit request.
length_signal_investigation.separate_finding_not_asked_for: Gating the panic handler so that cargo test runs surfaces a pre-existing failure their suite could never report: bm25::tests::exact_match_scores_high expects above 0.85 and gets exactly 0.400000. The cause is arithmetic, not the test. max_raw accumulates K1 + 1.0 per term, the bound as term frequency tends to infinity, while an exact match achieves tf_norm of exactly 1.0 per term when doc_len equals avg_dl. With K1 = 1.5 the ratio is 1 / 2.5 = 0.4, so a verbatim answer scores 0.4 on a signal meant to run to 1.0 and the 0.15-weighted lexical term can contribute at most 0.06 of the composite. Reported rather than changed: altering their normalisation would change scoring semantics across the network, which is their decision and not a side effect of a test fix.
length_signal_investigation.contributions_prepared_not_sent: Two local branches against the baseline clone: fix/cargo-test-panic-handler, gating #[panic_handler] behind #[cfg(not(test))] and #![no_std] behind cfg_attr so their 20 unit tests run, and experiment/length-variants carrying the three length signals behind cargo features. Nothing has been pushed, forked, or opened as a pull request.

handover_contract.split: Agreed with Codex's proposal: this side finishes and freezes the harness, corpora and acceptance thresholds; Codex builds the hybrid scorer against them; this side reviews the results independently. The reason is the central failure of the registration series. One author wrote both the scorer and every corpus that judged it, so the corpora agreed with the rules because the same blind spots produced both. Separating author from evaluator is a structural fix rather than a process courtesy.
handover_contract.amendment_1_thresholds_frozen_first: The thresholds are committed BEFORE the hybrid is measured, not chosen after. A bar set once the result is known is the same error as authoring your own evaluator, applied to the bar.
handover_contract.amendment_2_resolution_limit_stated: The held-out corpus has 30 pairs and 20 of them defeat both architectures, so the measurable headroom is 10 pairs and a single pair is 3.3 percent. It cannot resolve small differences. Treat a change of one pair as noise; a claim of improved generalisation needs at least +3, meaning 12 of 30 or better. This limit is stated rather than left for the reader to infer from the sample size.

frozen_bar.TestLengthBehaviour: 4 of 4, no tolerance. Both directions must hold.
frozen_bar.TestHeldOutPairAccuracy: at least 9 of 30 to pass; at least 12 of 30 to claim improved generalisation
frozen_bar.TestScorerRanksCandidatePools: at least 8 separated, at most 1 tie, at most 1 inversion, worst separation at least -0.0459
frozen_bar.TestGeneratedPairRankingQuality: at most 9 inverted and at most 9 below the 0.15 floor of 375
frozen_bar.TestRegistrationMarginsHoldOnBothEngines: all 88 factual pairs clear their minimum margins under both wazero engines. Non-negotiable: these margins are the registered evidence.
frozen_bar.TestSyntheticOrdinalFactualPairs: weakest synthetic factual margin at least 0.206250; a change in the ordinal Spearman must be recorded with its cause rather than silently repinned
frozen_bar.TestEngineScoresAgree: no divergence outside the recorded allowlist
frozen_bar.TestNearBoundaryEngineExposure: at most 90 diverging pairs and 0 verdict flips at the 0.15 floor
frozen_bar.TestArtifactContract: artifact identity, isolated clean builds and platform digests all reproduce

design_constraints_from_measured_failure: No hard zeros on a signal that can fire on a correct answer. Registration 98 lost three cases because two rules moved from capping at 0.49 to returning zero, and a zero can only ever remove a win that a cap might have kept. Prefer a multiplicative discount on a semantically grounded base.
One change per registration. Bundling two in registration 98 destroyed the ability to attribute the regression to either.

A rising local number is evidence about the properties that corpus encodes and about nothing else. Across four registrations local ranking improved monotonically while the scored result went 31, 31, 31, 28.

quantisation_finding.source: Measured through the third-party harness in zkasuran/telegraph-salience-scorer, MIT licensed, run on its own 40-case benchmark and 12-case attack suite. That module is the active champion for eight intents at registrations 26 to 33, is 8.4 KB, no_std with no imports, and reports 32 of 32 fixture wins. Its harness accepts an arbitrary second wasm, so it evaluates ours on cases authored by someone with no knowledge of our rules.
quantisation_finding.headline: Over the 80 benchmark scores, ours produces 30 distinct values and theirs produces 75. Ours repeats 0.3000 eighteen times, 0.0000 nine times, 0.1500 six times, 0.4900 six times and 0.7812 five times. 0.30 and 0.49 are literal score.min() ceilings in evaluate, so the scorer quantises onto its own clamp values.
quantisation_finding.head_to_head: Their benchmark: theirs margin 0.6847 with 40 of 40 correct rankings, ours margin 0.3148 with 33 of 40.
attack_suite_failures: direction-flip: attack 0.4031 scores ABOVE honest 0.3000. Independent confirmation of the relation-direction defect.
negation-insert: attack 0.4250 above honest 0.3071. Inserting a negation raises our score.
word-order-swap: exact tie at 0.8500. Swapping argument order is invisible.
stopword-spam and empty-ish: expected near zero, both score exactly 0.3000, which is the clamp rather than a judgement.
shotgun-candidates: 0.7337 against honest 0.7812, below but not far enough below to pass their gate.
quantisation_finding.why_this_matters_more_than_the_individua: It connects five observations that were recorded separately and never linked. The authorship_entity_swap tie at exactly 0.490000, the three misspelling pairs tying at exactly 0.000000, the word-order tie at 0.8500, the Stage 2 score_stddev of 0.2977 against the salience author's 0.391, and the fact that five defect fixes moved Telegraph's per-case count by zero. All are the same structural property: when a scorer's primary discrimination mechanism is a hard ceiling, its output collapses onto a handful of values, ties become frequent by construction, and adding further rules only moves answers between the same few buckets. The information is not in the score to begin with.
quantisation_finding.corroboration_from_the_other_author: Their README states that a flat-scoring or all-or-nothing module is rejected by the node, and they apply a deliberate smoothstep contrast curve for that reason. Their score_stddev is 0.391 against ours at 0.2977.
quantisation_finding.necessary_but_possibly_not_sufficient: Continuity alone is not the whole fix. An earlier attempt to relax the 0.49 ceiling into an order-preserving band turned a tie into an inversion, because the pre-clamp ordering was already wrong: the wrong answer scored 0.795000 against the correct answer's 0.781250. So the underlying signals must be right as well as continuous. Quantisation is what makes fine distinctions inexpressible; it is not what makes the coarse ones wrong.
quantisation_finding.design_consequence: The next scorer should compute continuous signals and apply graded multiplicative discounts, rather than deriving discrimination from hard ceilings. That is independent of the structural role-binding work and has to come first, because role binding expressed through another clamp would land in the same buckets.

heldout_generalisation_finding.design: 30 pairs across 10 shapes, every one deliberately chosen because no rule in scorer.rs was written to detect it: process reversal, comparative reframing, misspellings, scope overclaiming, hedged-correct against confident-wrong, definition inversion, register shifts, list membership, temporal order and causal direction. Each row states why its wrong answer is false, because two earlier corpora here shipped rows whose wrong answer was actually true.
heldout_generalisation_finding.result: Ours orders 9 of 30 correctly. On corpora authored in this repository the same build orders 10 of 10 ranking pools and 366 of 375 generated pairs. 30 percent on unseen shapes against near-perfect on seen ones is the explanation for the registration series: the scorer does not generalise, it recognises the specific defect shapes someone wrote a rule for. That is why five defect fixes moved Telegraph's per-case count by zero.
heldout_generalisation_finding.champion_on_the_same_corpus: 3 of 30. Neither architecture handles these shapes and 20 of the 30 defeat both. Ours ordered 7 that the champion did not; the champion ordered 1 that ours did not.
heldout_generalisation_finding.why_both_fail: These shapes invert meaning while preserving surface form. 'Photosynthesis converts carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen' against its exact reverse has near-identical embeddings and near-total token overlap. Cosine similarity measures topical relatedness, not logical structure, so it cannot separate 'A causes B' from 'B causes A'; a lexical rule engine cannot either unless someone wrote a rule for that specific inversion.
heldout_generalisation_finding.four_of_our_misses_are_exact_ties: typo_brazil, typo_capital_australia, typo_mitochondria and temporal_order_flight all score good and bad identically, and process_direction_digestion ties too. A misspelled correct answer and a correctly spelled wrong one are indistinguishable. Ties lose a case exactly as inversions do.
heldout_generalisation_finding.three_corpora_three_verdicts: Telegraph's hidden fixtures: champion 32 of 32, ours 31 of 32. Our ranking pools: ours 8 of 10 separated, champion 2 of 10. These held-out shapes: ours 9 of 30, champion 3 of 30. No one of those is the measure of a judge, and each was built by someone who could only see their own blind spots. Quoting any single one as a verdict is the error recorded under overfitting_finding.
heldout_generalisation_finding.ratchet: minHeldOutOrdered is set to the measured 9. It was first written as 21 before measuring, which is the same error as setting a floor from hope; the file now records the fact rather than the aspiration.
heldout_generalisation_finding.champion_not_vendored: The comparison runs only when OATHCAST_CHAMPION_WASM points at a local build, and says loudly when it does not run rather than skipping quietly. A path that is set but unreadable fails rather than skips, and the harness rejects a projection-mode build by checking that a low-overlap paraphrase separates from unrelated text by at least 0.25.
heldout_generalisation_finding.indicated_direction: The gap both architectures share, meaning reversal under high surface similarity, is structural rather than semantic: argument-order inversion, dropped negation, reactant and product exchange. Those are checkable properties and are the kind of thing a discrete rule can express and an embedding cannot. That is a more promising direction than either more entity rules or more embedding weight, and unlike the fixture-shaped work it would generalise by construction.

ranking_benchmark.purpose: Measures the module as a judge rather than a fixture-passer, after Telegraph's team clarified that the module's value is how well it ranks miners rather than whether it becomes the canonical script.
ranking_benchmark.metric: separation = worst correct candidate minus best wrong candidate, per pool, against the real WASM through wazero
fixed_ranking_defects: negation_polarity: 'Yes, K2 is the tallest mountain on Earth' (wrong) scored 0.862500 while 'Everest is indeed Earth's highest peak' (correct) scored 0.370000, a separation of -0.4925. The wrong answer now scores 0.000000 and the pool separates. See entity_binding_fix.
known_ranking_defects: shared_token_distractor: 'Portuguese is spoken in Portugal', wrong for the question asked, outranks the correct 'Brazilians speak Portuguese' by 0.045833.
authorship_entity_swap: a correct loosely-worded answer and a wrong answer are both pinned to the 0.49 ambiguity ceiling, a separation of exactly 0.000000, so the pool cannot be ordered.
ranking_benchmark.common_cause: Lexical overlap with the ground truth outweighed correct entity binding, so copying the truth's frame and swapping the entity beat a faithful paraphrase. Addressed for the unanchored case by question_entity_substituted; and for the anchored case by question_entity_slot_substituted. All ten pools now separate; the remaining defect class, predicate substitution, is not represented in these pools and is tracked in generated_pair_scoreboard.
ranking_benchmark.scope: Handcrafted development pools. Not Telegraph fixtures and not a claim about hidden Stage 2 cases.
ranking_benchmark.engine: wazero interpreter. The default compiler backend was measured scoring two candidates differently on linux/amd64, so the benchmark uses the engine that agrees across every os/arch/engine combination tested. See runtime_determinism.

runtime_determinism.finding: The same module bytes score two inputs differently under wazero v1.12.0's amd64 compiler backend than under its interpreter or its arm64 compiler. Registration pins this module by Keccak over raw bytes, so identical bytes are supposed to imply identical scores; on one of six measured configurations they do not.

detail: negation_polarity/affirmative_paraphrase: amd64 compiler 0.490000, every other configuration 0.370000
no_longer_divergent: negation_polarity/unrelated diverged 0.490000 against 0.150000 on the 42,790-byte build. The entity-binding fix now scores it 0.000000 on both engines, because the answer names a subject foreign to the question, so the input no longer reaches the divergent path. The allowlist retains it as a ceiling rather than an expectation.

telegraph_response.substance: Telegraph confirmed they run a single validator today, so the divergence does not affect them much yet; they intend to move to deterministic execution as they scale to multiple validators, and have not done so because deterministic execution is roughly 10 to 50 times slower.
telegraph_response.what_it_resolves: Cross-miner fairness is not currently at risk. With one validator every miner is scored on the same machine under the same engine, so two identical answers receive identical scores. The multi-validator inconsistency concern is deferred rather than present.
telegraph_response.what_it_does_not_resolve: Whether the scores their validator computes match the scores measured here. Validator count is irrelevant to that: it is a question about agreement between their machine and ours, not between two of theirs. Not directly confirmed, since they did not name the runtime.
telegraph_response.measured_direction_of_effect: In all 84 diverging generated pairs the compiler raised the correct answer to exactly 0.490000 and never moved the wrong answer, so every margin widened. The mechanism is not a preference for correct answers: it pulls low scores up to 0.490000 regardless of correctness, and these templates make the correct answer the lexically distant, lower-scoring one. In the curated pools the opposite case occurred once, where a wrong answer rose from 0.150000 to 0.490000 and narrowed a margin. Current net exposure on the measured sample is therefore favourable to neutral, not adverse, but the sign is a property of which side scores low rather than a safety property.
telegraph_response.consequence_for_us: The exposure cannot be closed by waiting for Telegraph, because they have said they will not change execution until multi-validator scaling. defect_1.asymmetry: Introducing a modifier the truth lacks is penalised; omitting one the truth has is not. Omission is ordinary paraphrase: against 'Curie is the first woman to win a Nobel Prize.', the answer 'Curie won a Nobel Prize before any other woman.' drops the ordinal and stays correct. Matching is per exact token, so a truth saying 'second' does not license an answer saying 'third'.

defect_2.name: weather classifier over-trigger

defect_2.residual_not_fixed: A lowercase weather word used non-meteorologically still routes a binary question down the weather path, so 'Is ice less dense than water?' is still treated as a weather question. ordinal_and_classifier_fix.not_addressed: The 9 remaining generated inversions substitute one superlative for another: 'the longest river in Africa' becomes 'the deepest river in Africa'. relation_mismatch_contradiction_fix.reverted: Reverted on 2026-08-19 after registration 98 won 28 of 32 where the three previous builds all won 31. relation_mismatch_contradiction_fix.defect: A hard ceiling flattened distinct-quality answers onto one value. Against the truth 'Hamlet was written by Shakespeare.', both 'It is Shakespeare that is associated with Hamlet.' (correct) and 'Shakespeare and Marlowe were contemporaries, but Hamlet was written by Marlowe.' (wrong) scored exactly 0.490000. Telegraph's Stage 2 requires the good answer to rank above the bad one, so an equal score loses the case exactly as an inversion does.
relation_mismatch_contradiction_fix.why_relaxing_the_ceiling_was_the_wrong_f: Measured pre-clamp, the wrong answer scored 0.795000 against the correct answer's 0.781250, because naming Shakespeare anywhere in the answer satisfied anchor support while the operative relation bound Marlowe. Mapping scores into an order-preserving band below the ceiling would therefore have converted the tie into an inversion. The ceiling was concealing an inversion rather than causing the tie, which is also why an earlier attempt to relax it drove the margin negative.
relation_mismatch_contradiction_fix.how_the_discriminator_was_found: Both answers trip connector ambiguity and directed-relation ambiguity, and both trip unexpected_directed_relation, so none of those separates them. Only relation_mismatch is true for the wrong answer and false for the correct one.
relation_mismatch_contradiction_fix.fix: relation_mismatch now sets contradicted rather than feeding ambiguous_or_stuffed, so it short-circuits to zero before any ceiling applies. The signal earns that treatment on its own terms: it requires the answer's entity pairing to disagree with the ground truth's and a novel entity to be introduced after a contrast word, which describes asserting that someone else did it rather than being unclear about who did.
relation_mismatch_contradiction_fix.principle: A ceiling is the right response to 'I cannot tell what you claimed'. It is the wrong response to 'you claimed something false'. Treating both identically is what made two answers of opposite correctness indistinguishable.

slot_substitution_fix.defect: With an anchor present and satisfied, exchanging the entity behind the same preposition went unpunished. Against the question 'What language is spoken in Brazil?' and the truth 'Portuguese is spoken in Brazil.', the wrong answer 'Portuguese is spoken in Portugal.' scored 0.804167 while the correct paraphrase 'Brazilians speak Portuguese.' scored 0.758333. The anchor is 'Portuguese', the wrong answer contains it, so anchor support was satisfied and nothing objected to the country being swapped.
slot_substitution_fix.why_the_existing_rule_could_not_be_exten: question_entity_substituted is gated to the case where no binding anchor exists. Removing that gate fails six tests, because dropping a question entity while naming an unfamiliar one is something correct answers do routinely. The measured false positives were 'The capital is not Berlin but Paris.' which names an entity in order to deny it, 'ECMWF expects rain during that hour.' which attributes a source, and answers supplying an alias the truth does not spell out.
slot_substitution_fix.discriminator: The slot. The truth says 'spoken in Brazil' and the wrong answer says 'spoken in Portugal', the same preceding token with the entity exchanged. 'not Berlin' does not match 'of France', and a sentence-initial source attribution has no preceding token at all. So the test is that the truth's bound entity is absent from the answer and a foreign entity appears behind the very token that preceded the bound entity in the truth.
two_corrections_during_implementation: The first version required the slot token to satisfy is_fact_relation_or_filler, which silently did nothing here because 'in' is not on that list, so 'spoken in Brazil' never registered a slot and the rule never fired. Slot equality is what discriminates, so admissibility only needs to exclude an empty predecessor and another entity.

The rule initially applied to weather questions too, where it duplicated context_conflict and did it worse: it caught 'in Abuja' but not 'in abuja' or 'in the city of abuja', turning consistent handling into capitalisation-dependent handling. It is now the non-weather analogue of the context-constraint check, which is only populated for weather questions.

separation_rubric_finding.summary: The rubric changed and inverted a lesson this repository had recorded as settled. Under average separation, a cap that shaves 0.03 keeps the win and earns almost no margin, so a confident defect has to land low rather than merely below its pair.

separation_transform_attempted_and_rever.the_idea: The champion's output is very nearly binary, about 0.998 for answers it accepts and about 0.01 for the rest, with roughly a hundredth of spread inside the low band. Its author describes this directly: take a hard step for separation, then add back two percent of the raw score so ranking survives inside each band. A smooth score cannot average a large separation however well it orders, and registration 506 won 11 of 12 cases on ordering while averaging 0.1929, so this looked like the whole gap.
separation_transform_attempted_and_rever.simulated_gain: Applied to recorded scores, a hard step at 0.40 took the core corpus from +0.3856 to +0.6610, the ranking pools from +0.5373 to +0.8927, the structural corpus from +0.2000 to +0.3960 and the weather corpus from +0.4795 to +0.7446, with the inversion count unchanged in all four, since a monotonic transform cannot reorder anything. Agreement was provably unaffected for the same reason.
separation_transform_attempted_and_rever.why_it_was_reverted: It amplifies our errors by the same factor as our judgements. The hard step took the count of generated pairs with a margin under the 0.15 floor from 9 to 135 of 375, because a good and a bad answer on the same side of the threshold collapse to within a hundredth. A finite-width ramp, swept and set at 0.24, reduced that to 79 but broke three cases in the published fixture contract: an answer that merely echoes the question rose to 0.8637 against a recorded ceiling of 0.49, a 51% answer against a 90% truth rose to 0.9919 against 0.61, and a partial answer rose to 0.7637 against 0.70.
separation_transform_attempted_and_rever.the_reason_it_cannot_be_tuned_away: Those three answers have raw scores of roughly 0.50, 0.60 and 0.55, and a good answer has roughly 0.85. Keeping raw 0.60 below 0.61 while pushing raw 0.85 high requires a ramp so wide that no amplification remains. The champion can afford a near-binary output because its raw judgement already separates 0.99 from 0.01; ours overlaps, correct answers running 0.25 to 0.98 and wrong ones 0.10 to 0.62. Amplification is not a shortcut past that overlap.
separation_transform_attempted_and_rever.what_this_makes_the_next_task: Create the headroom in the raw score first. The named blockers are concrete: an answer that copies the question scores about 0.50, a probability off by 39 points scores about 0.60, and a partial answer scores about 0.55. Push those down and the transform becomes available, worth an estimated 1.5 to 1.7 times on average separation.

output_transform_second_attempt.what_changed_first: Two raw-headroom fixes made the transform viable where it had been impossible. A material probability disagreement, more than a quarter of the scale, now takes a 0.30 ceiling: against a 90 percent truth, a 51 percent answer fell from 0.5807 to 0.2651. An answer that is a question rather than an answer now takes a 0.20 ceiling: the fixture's question-copy case fell from 0.4891 to 0.1745. Both were named as the specific blockers when the first attempt was reverted.
output_transform_second_attempt.swept_and_measured: With those in place a ramp at threshold 0.48, width 0.24 respected all three recorded fixture ceilings for the first time, and lifted the core corpus from +0.4025 to +0.5535, the ranking pools from +0.5373 to +0.8564, the structural corpus from +0.2000 to +0.3037 and the weather corpus from +0.4962 to +0.6722.
output_transform_second_attempt.why_it_is_still_not_shipped: It took the count of generated pairs below the 0.15 margin floor from 9 to 96 of 375, concentrated entirely in two categories, identity_binary at 42 of 45 and negation_polarity at 42 of 45. Raising the retained raw share from 2 percent to 30 percent did not move that count. Raising the threshold above the ceiling constants did not move it either, and took identity_binary to 45 of 45.
output_transform_second_attempt.the_interaction_that_causes_it: Our ceiling constants are 0.20, 0.30, 0.40 and 0.49, and a deliberately capped answer therefore lands on a clamp value. In identity_binary the wrong answer is the ground truth with its subject swapped, which we detect and cap; the correct answer is a terse indirect restatement which also scores modestly. The two end up adjacent and on the same side of any threshold, so the ramp maps them to nearly the same value however it is placed. The transform cannot separate answers that our raw judgement places next to each other, and on these two categories it does not.
output_transform_second_attempt.what_would_make_it_work: The correct terse answer in those categories has to score high, not merely higher. That is the same finding as the core discrimination work: our wrong answers are now reasonably low and our correct answers are not high enough. Until a terse correct answer scores near 0.9 rather than near 0.6, amplification has nothing to amplify.
output_transform_second_attempt.status: Reverted for the second time. Both attempts, their measurements and the reasons are recorded rather than dropped, because the shape of the failure is the useful part.

positive_evidence_path.why: Every rule in this module was a deduction, so a correct answer earned nothing for being correct. On the core discrimination corpus our correct answers averaged 0.6483 where the live champion places accepted answers near 0.998, and on the generated corpus a terse correct answer landed adjacent to the clamp value its wrong counterpart had been capped onto. That adjacency is why two output transforms could not separate them: a monotonic transform cannot pull apart two scores the judgement placed side by side.
positive_evidence_path.first_hypothesis_was_wrong: The plan was a floor for answers that affirm the truth's claims. Implemented alone it changed nothing, average correct-answer score identical to four decimal places, because the low-scoring correct answers were not missing credit, they were being actively capped. Instrumenting the blend against the final score showed correct answers blending at 0.79, 0.72, 0.71 and 0.94 and being cut to 0.25, 0.45, 0.47 and 0.49.
positive_evidence_path.the_real_defect: Two correct answers were capped for MISSING_BINARY_ANSWER. Asked whether there was a thunderstorm, the correct answer 'Thunder and lightning were observed over Lagos in that window.' was treated as not answering, because polarity was inferred only from yes, true, likely, expected and occurred. Naming the phenomenon is how a forecast says it happened.

changes.concept_implies_polarity: A weather concept asserted with no negation anywhere in the text reads as affirmative, along with fell, fall, observed, recorded, measured, detected and reported. Scoped to weather questions.
changes.interrogatives_assert_nothing: explicit_polarity returns Unknown for text ending in a question mark, so the fixture's question copy keeps tripping the ceiling it is meant to trip rather than reading as a positive answer because it names precipitation.
changes.positive_evidence_floor: 0.90 when the answer contradicts none of the truth's claims and affirms at least two of polarity, figures within tolerance, weather concepts, probability and anchor support. Applied only on weather questions, only when no ceiling fired, and only when the answer is falsifiable.
changes.unfalsifiable_guard: The floor is withheld from answers containing possible, variable, always, sometimes, may, might, could and similar. Without it the evasive 'Weather in Lagos is variable and precipitation is always possible at some point.' rose from 0.4836 to 0.9189, above a correct answer's paired score.

three_regressions_measured_and_fixed.wrong_answer_lifted_on_a_non_weather_cas: Unscoped, the floor lifted a wrong answer on 'Which mountain is the highest above sea level?' to 0.90 and inverted a pair that had been ordered correctly.
